market_mood: A hot October CPI print knocked stocks lower and has economists now expecting another Fed hike in December, while oil slid as Trump played down the chance of fresh strikes on Iran. Energy is the week's worst sector, tech is still digesting the Nvidia headlines, and defensive/rate-sensitive names are in focus.
self_check: My oil & energy calls have been a disaster lately (0 for 13 in the last ten run-days) and my 'high' confidence calls are badly negative, so today I used no high confidence, kept energy to one small low-confidence idea, and leaned on merger and geopolitics setups that have worked.

picks.reason: October CPI came in hot and a Reuters poll of economists now expects the Fed to hike once more in December, which pushes long-bond yields up and prices down.
The DOJ is expected to weigh in on the Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern merger within weeks, and the deal spread should narrow if the opinion is neutral or favorable.
GFL rejected a $52/share private-equity offer and ended its strategic review, removing the takeover premium that had supported the stock.
Missile defense interceptors stay in demand as Houthi attacks and Gulf defense build-outs continue.

watchlist_notes.note: Opened lower after a hotter-than-expected October CPI, with a December rate hike now the base case in a Reuters poll.
Tech is down 5.6% on the week; higher-for-longer rates plus Nvidia headline risk keep the Nasdaq the most exposed index.
Dow drags from Boeing's 5% commercial workforce cut and broad inflation worries.
No major company news; a commentary piece notes the stock's 15% rally and buyback-driven story.
A Fed official calling AI data-center spending 'old-fashioned overheating' adds to scrutiny of hyperscaler capex.
Fell nearly 7% on the CEO scandal and a House Democratic leader pushing for tighter China chip restrictions, though chip peers bounced.
Starting Black Friday promotions Nov. 19 with Alexa-powered tools; analysts argue cancelled data centers favor cash-rich hyperscalers.
Named alongside Nvidia and Micron in a $26B investment into a big AI customer, and tied to the Anthropic IPO story valuing it near $1.4T.
Still recovering from a near-$10B legal charge; its AI assistant launch is flagged as the next catalyst.
A December hike would support net interest income; payments unit got a best-in-class biometric ranking.
Gold eased ahead of CPI; a hotter print and a likely December hike are a near-term headwind.
Hot CPI and a Reuters poll pointing to another December hike are negative for long-duration Treasuries.

top_buys.pitch: Hot CPI plus a likely December hike means long bonds stay under pressure.
top_buys.why: October inflation came in above expectations and a Reuters poll of economists now sees the Fed raising rates once more in December. Long-dated Treasuries are the most sensitive asset to that shift, and the repricing of rate expectations tends to play out over weeks, not a single session. TLT is a low-volatility, liquid way to express that view.
top_buys.risks: If the next jobs report is weak or Fed officials push back on a December hike, yields could fall fast and TLT would rally.
top_buys.watch: Fed speakers this week and the December FOMC meeting.

top_buys.pitch: A DOJ opinion on the Union Pacific merger in coming weeks could close the deal discount.
top_buys.why: Reports say the Justice Department will give its view on the Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern combination within weeks, the key remaining regulatory overhang. Merger-arb spreads on this deal have stayed wide on antitrust fear, so a neutral or supportive DOJ stance would lift NSC toward deal terms. My merger-themed calls have been my most consistent category.
top_buys.risks: A hostile DOJ filing would widen the spread sharply and knock NSC down; the STB process also remains long and uncertain.
top_buys.watch: Any DOJ statement or filing on the merger in the next few weeks.

top_buys.pitch: The takeover premium is gone after GFL rejected $52/share and ended its review.
top_buys.why: GFL turned down a private-equity consortium's $52-a-share offer and formally ended its strategic review, which removes the bid support that had held the shares up. Stocks that end a sale process typically drift lower for weeks as event-driven holders exit. The waste sector is otherwise fairly valued, so there's little else to catch the stock.
top_buys.risks: A new or improved bidder could return, or management could announce buybacks or asset sales that support the shares.
top_buys.watch: Whether any consortium returns with a higher bid or GFL announces capital-return plans.

top_buys.pitch: Missile defense interceptors stay in demand as Houthi attacks and Gulf defense build-outs continue.
top_buys.why: The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting Houthi missiles and drones, and Gulf states are formalizing a joint military command. That sustains demand for air and missile defense systems where RTX is a leading supplier. These restocking cycles tend to show up in orders over quarters.
top_buys.risks: A broad Iran de-escalation or budget gridlock in a divided Congress could slow order flow.
top_buys.watch: Foreign military sales announcements from Gulf states.

summary.big_story: A hotter-than-expected October CPI sent stocks lower and has economists expecting another Fed rate hike in December, even as oil fell on cooling Iran war talk.
summary.top_pick: Short long-duration Treasuries via TLT, since a December hike and sticky inflation argue for higher long yields.
summary.watch: Fed speakers' reaction to CPI, the DOJ's opinion on the Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern deal, and whether oil keeps sliding as Iran tensions cool.
